matters.MatterTitle: Approve a resolution directing the City Manager to establish a reporting and tracking process, provide quarterly reports to Council, provide updates regarding legislative efforts, convene a sub-quorum of Council Members to guide legislative objectives, address concerns from community organizations, and establish a community advisory group related to the implementation of the No Wrong Door initiative.

Approve an ordinance waiving or reimbursing certain fees related to Austin Sister Cities International's Austin-Taichung 40th Anniversary Celebration held at the Asian American Resource Center on September 19, 2026.

Approve a resolution directing the City Manager to work with the Capital Area Metropolitan Planning Organization, the Texas Department of Transportation, and other partners to prioritize safety, walking, biking, and transit in proposed Parmer Lane (Farm to Market Road 734) improvements, and to advocate for a full environmental review of any proposal for the corridor.

Approve a resolution appointing Juan Garza, Veronica Castro de Barrera, and Kammy Horne as the Community Expert Director members of the Austin Transit Partnership (ATP) Board of Directors to serve terms beginning in January 2025, as recommended by the ATP Board Vacancy Nominating Committee. Funding: This item has no fiscal impact.
Discussion and possible action on social services strategy that will include issue area, compliance, and policy discussion.

Approve the minutes of the Austin City Council work session meeting of September 22, 2026, regular meeting of September 24, 2026, work session meeting of October 6, 2026, and regular meeting of October 8, 2026.

Authorize negotiation and execution of all documents and instruments necessary or desirable to acquire, on behalf of Austin Transportation and Public Works, a right of way and two-part temporary working space easements needed for the 2020 Bond Substandard Streets Johnny Morris Road project. The proposed acquisition consists of approximately 2.415 acres (105,184 square feet) of right of way and approximately 1,260 square feet of temporary working space easement in two parts (1,010 square feet and 250 square feet), situated in the James Burleson Survey No. 19, Abstract No. 4, City of Austin, Travis County, Texas, and being out of a called 20.00-acre tract described in a Warranty Deed from Anthony C. Chen and Gloria Chen to Austin Ultiplex, LLC, recorded in Document No. 2014141999, Official Public Records of Travis County, generally located at 5525 Johnny Morris Road, Austin, Texas 78724, from Austin Ultiplex, LLC, a Texas limited liability company, for a total amount not to exceed $153,000, including closing costs. Funding: $153,000 is available in the Capital Budget of Austin Transportation and Public Works.

Conduct a public hearing and consider an ordinance granting floodplain variances for the property located at 1213 Fort Branch Boulevard from certain floodplain regulations prescribed by City Code for the construction of two single-family dwelling units within the 25-year and 100-year floodplains of Fort Branch Creek; establishing the conditions for the variances; and providing an expiration date for the variances. Funding: This item has no fiscal impact.

Approve a resolution authorizing the filing of eminent domain proceedings and payment to acquire the property interests needed in support of Austin Water’s NW Tarrytown Wastewater Pipeline Renewal Project, for the public use of rehabilitating aging and deteriorating wastewater infrastructure, including replacing and upsizing approximately 2,400 LF of 8-inch and 10-inch concrete wastewater pipeline within the Tarrytown Neighborhood requiring the acquisition of a three-part wastewater easement consisting of approximately 0.0878 of one acre (3,826 square foot) of wastewater easement, in three parts, and the acquisition of a temporary working space easement consisting of 0.0140 of one acre (609 square foot), both easements being out of the Daniel J. Gilbert Survey, Abstract Number 313, in Travis County, Texas, being a portion of Lot 21, West Park Place Amended, a subdivision of record in Book 73, Page 31, Plat Records, Travis County, Texas, said Lot 21 conveyed to Tarryhollow Homeowners’ Association, Inc. by Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions dated August 20, 1975, as recorded in Volume 5246, Page 2261, Deed Records, Travis County, Texas, currently appraised at $4,086, subject to an increase in value based on updated appraisals, a Special Commissioners’ award, negotiated settlement, or judgment. The owner of the needed property is Tarryhollow Homeowners’ Association, Inc. The property is located at 3212 Tarryhollow Drive, Austin, Texas 78703. The general route of the project is in the Tarrytown Neighborhood, between Pecos Street and Exposition Boulevard, Austin, Texas 78703. Funding: $4,086 is available in the Capital Budget of Austin Water.

Authorize negotiation and execution of all documents and instruments necessary or desirable to acquire a parcel in fee simple, an access easement, and a sidewalk, trail, and recreational easement on behalf of Austin Parks and Recreation for the Rutland to Northgate Trail project. The acquisition consists of a fee simple parcel of approximately 1.154 acres (50,255 square feet), an access easement of approximately 0.1188 acres (5,173 square feet), and a sidewalk, trail, and recreational easement of approximately 0.8154 acres (35,519 square feet) generally located at 9511 Metric Blvd., Austin, Texas 78758 from Butler Broadcasting Company, Ltd., for a total amount not to exceed $5,481,865 including closing costs. Funding: $5,481,865 is available in the Capital Budget of Austin Parks and Recreation.

Approve an ordinance recertifying Guadalupe Neighborhood Development Corporation as a Community Land Trust and granting the corporation a property tax exemption on certain properties. Funding: The tax exemption covers the City portion of property taxes, resulting in unrealized revenue, and will aid in the development and preservation of long-term affordable housing.

Authorize a contract for a statistical analysis system, analytics software support, and maintenance, used for business intelligence analysis and consumption and billing data reporting, for Austin Energy with Executive Information Systems LLC, for an initial term of one year in an estimated amount of $96,000 with up to four one-year extension options each in an estimated amount of $96,000 for a total contract amount not to exceed $480,000. Funding: $88,000 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budget of Austin Energy. Funding for the remaining contract term is contingent upon available funding in future budgets.

Authorize a contract for uniform and shop towel rental and laundering services for all City departments with Cintas Corporation No. 2 d/b/a Cintas Fire 636525 or Cintas First Aid & Safety or Cintas, for an initial term of two years in an estimated amount of $750,000 with up to three one-year extension options each in an estimated amount of $375,000 for a total contract amount not to exceed $1,875,000. Funding: $675,000 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budget of Austin Fleet Mobility Services. $1,200,000 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budgets of various City departments. Funding for the remaining contract term is contingent upon available funding in future budgets.

Authorize a contract for the one-time purchase of three portable handheld Raman spectroscopy analyzers, used to conduct preliminary narcotics testing and perform non-contact forensic analysis of various unknown substances, for Austin Police with Anton Paar USA, Inc., in an amount not to exceed $98,175. Funding: $98,175 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budget of Austin Police.

Authorize a contract for Infor Public Sector software maintenance and support, used to manage water distribution system assets and work orders, for Austin Water with DLT Solutions LLC d/b/a DLT Solutions, for an initial term of one year in an estimated amount of $393,300 with up to two one-year extension options each in variable amounts for a total contract amount not to exceed $1,252,200. Funding: $393,300 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budget of Austin Water. Funding for the remaining contract term is contingent upon available funding in future budgets.

Approve a resolution to commit funds of up to $1,000,000 for the design and construction of a dedicated center-running transit lane at Dean Keeton Street and Interstate Highway-35 as a transit betterment to be incorporated in the Texas Department of Transportation's Interstate Highway-35 Capital Express Central Project. Funding: $1,000,000 is available in the Capital Budget of Austin Transportation and Public Works.

Authorize five contracts for interior and exterior painting services at City facilities for all City departments with Corza Construction LLC; Fanar 1 Enterprise LLC d/b/a Fanar 1 Enterprise; JNA Painting & Contracting Company, Inc.; Omega Industries Inc.; and Prestige Building Group, LLC, each for an initial term of two years in an estimated amount of $3,183,000 with up to three one-year extension options each in an estimated amount of $1,591,500 for a total contract amount not to exceed $7,957,500 divided between the contractors. Funding: $458,333 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budget of Austin Facility Management. $1,133,167 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budgets of various City departments. Funding for the remaining contract term is contingent upon available funding in future budgets.

Authorize a contract for biomass characterization testing, used to monitor the operational health of wastewater treatment plants, for Austin Water with Hydro Solutions, Inc. d/b/a Effluency, LLC, for a term of three years in an amount not to exceed $260,000. Funding: $79,445 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budget of Austin Water. Funding for the remaining contract term is contingent upon available funding.

Approve an ordinance amending the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Austin Fire Department Operating Budget Special Revenue Fund (Ordinance No. 20260812-007) to accept and appropriate $90,087 in grant funds from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Assistance to Firefighters Grant for Peer Support Certification training and required overtime. Funding: $90,087 is available from FEMA. A City funding match of $13,513 is required and available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budget of Austin Fire.

Authorize a contract for construction services for the West Congress (Radam/St. Elmo) Water and Wastewater Pipeline Renewal Project for Austin Water with Facilities Rehabilitation Inc., in the amount of $2,837,732 plus a $283,774 contingency for a total contract amount not to exceed $3,121,506. Funding: $3,121,506 is available in the Capital Budget of Austin Water.

Authorize 16 contracts for engineering services for the 2026 Small Scale General Civil Engineering Services Rotation List for various departments with Huitt-Zollars, Inc.; Lockwood, Andrews & Newnam, Inc.; DAVCAR, Inc. d/b/a DAVCAR Engineering Services; MWM Design Group; Johnson, Mirmiran & Thompson, Inc.; Stantec Consulting Services, Inc.; AECOM Technical Services, Inc.; Gannett Fleming, Inc.; Doucet & Associates, Inc.; BGE, Inc.; Aguirre & Fields, LP; Dunaway Associates, LLC; HVJ South Central Texas - M&J, Inc.; Edge Engineering, PLLC; LJA Engineering, Inc.; and Riley Mountain Engineering LLC, for a total contract amount not to exceed $17,000,000, divided among the firms. Funding: Availability of funding for an assignment will be verified in the requesting department’s Capital Budget before services are authorized.
Approve the minutes of the Austin City Council work session meeting of October 20, 2026, and regular meeting of October 22, 2026.

Authorize two contracts for calcium hypochlorite tablets and granules, used for cleaning and disinfection in water treatment operations, for Austin Water with Leslie's Poolmart Inc. d/b/a Leslie's Swimming Pool Supplies and Joseph G Pollard Co. Inc. d/b/a Pollardwater, each for an initial term of two years in an estimated amount of $240,000 with up to three one-year extension options each in an estimated amount of $120,000 for a total contract amount not to exceed $600,000, divided between the contractors. Funding: $110,000 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budget of Austin Water. Funding for the remaining contract term is contingent upon available funding in future budgets.

Authorize a contract for medical billing and coding services, to manage the medical billing revenue cycle and collect eligible revenue, for Austin Public Health with Transworld Systems Inc., for an initial term of one year with up to four one-year extension options for a total estimated revenue of $5,000,000. Funding: This item is projected to result in annual revenue of $1,000,000 in the Operating Budget of Austin Public Health. The contractor will be compensated at a rate of 5.10% of the total annual claims collected. Compensation will be deducted directly from the collected proceeds rather than issued as a separate payment.

Approve an ordinance dedicating revenue derived from the City’s portion of tax revenues that will be generated from Tax Increment Reinvestment Zone No. 21 to the City’s Housing Trust Fund and the City’s Parks Enhancement Fund, and requiring an annual report about those tax revenues. Funding: This item has no fiscal impact.

Approve the corrected minutes for the June 5, 2024; September 4, 2024; February 5, 2025; March 5, 2025; April 2, 2025; October 1, 2025; February 4, 2026, meetings and the May 22, 2024, Special Called Meeting of the Public Health Committee.
Approve the minutes for the October 7, 2026, meeting of the Public Health Committee.
Discussion and possible action on approving the Public Health Committee calendar for 2027.
Discussion and possible action on appointments to the Central Health Board of Managers.
Discussion regarding candidates for appointments to the Central Health Board of Managers. (Personnel matters - Section 551.074 of the Texas Government Code).
Identify items for future meetings.

Approve an ordinance amending City Code Title 4 (Business Regulation and Permit Requirements) to require kennel operators to make their outdoor spaces escape-proof and to create an offense and penalty. Funding: This item has no fiscal impact. The proposed amendment is intended for private boarding facilities and does not impact City facilities.

Approve an ordinance amending the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Austin Technology Services Operating Budget (Ordinance No. 20260812-007) to accept and appropriate $60,000 in grant funds from the Office of the Governor Public Safety Office for the Role-based Cybersecurity Training program. Funding: $60,000 is available from Office of the Governor Public Safety Office. A City funding match of $15,000 is required and available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budget of Austin Technology Services.

Approve the phase plan for Pease District Park under the existing Park Operations and Maintenance Agreement with the Pease Park Conservancy, expanding the Conservancy’s responsibilities for operations, maintenance, land management, programming, event coordination, and volunteer management beyond Kingsbury Commons to additional areas of Pease District Park to help offset City costs. Funding: This action has a positive fiscal impact by offsetting the City’s costs to maintain Pease District Park and will result in improved access for the general public.

Authorize negotiation and execution of an interlocal agreement with the Austin Independent School District to support Literacy First, a reading and tutoring intervention program, for a 12-month term through September 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $100,000, with four 12-month renewal options in amounts not to exceed $100,000 per renewal option, for a total agreement amount not to exceed $500,000. Funding: $100,000 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Austin Parks and Recreation Department Operating Budget. Funding for the agreement is contingent upon available funding in future budgets.

Approve an ordinance waiving or reimbursing certain fees related to the Village of Western Oaks' 4th of July Parade and Celebration held at the Dick Nichols District Park on July 4, 2026.

Authorize a contract for Microsoft Unified Support services to provide reactive and advisory support, training and readiness, and risk mitigation for Austin Technology Services with Microsoft Corp., for a term of three years in an amount not to exceed $5,000,000. Funding: $1,500,000 is available in the Operating Budget of Austin Technology Services. Funding for the remaining contract term is contingent upon available funding in future budgets.

Updates on Homeless Encampment Management initiative, which provides a coordinated approach to encampment response through outreach, enforcement, site management, and public space restoration efforts that connect people experiencing homelessness with supportive services while restoring public spaces and amenities. [David Gray, Director - Austin Homeless Strategies and Operations]
Approve the corrected minutes for the February 7, 2024, and November 6, 2024, meetings of the Public Health Committee.

Approve appointments and certain related waivers to boards and commissions, to Council committees and other intergovernmental bodies, and to public facility corporations; removal and replacement of members; and amendments to board and commission bylaws.
Approve a resolution directing the City Manager to develop and implement a targeted, commercial space, buy-down rental assistance program.
Discussion and possible action on social services strategy that will include solicitation overview, pay for performance, grants versus contracts and stakeholder engagement.
Approve the minutes for the September 23, 2026, meeting of the Climate, Water, Environment, and Parks Committee.

Approve a resolution that directs the City Manager to update the City’s Strategic Housing Blueprint to address updated housing production and preservation goals, include a data analysis, displacement and other strategies, consideration for a potential bond program, engage stakeholders and report back to Council.

Authorize contracts for the 2025 Job Order Contract Program with the following contractors: Jamail & Smith Construction, LP; Centennial Contractors Enterprises, Inc.; Spawglass Contractors, Inc.; RS Ellis, Inc. d/b/a Southwest Corporation; QA Construction Services, Inc.; Warden Construction Corporation; SDB, Inc. d/b/a SDB Contracting Services; Balfour Beatty Construction Group, Inc. d/b/a Balfour Beatty Construction, LLC; Basic IDIQ, Inc.; and Veliz Company, LLC, d/b/a Veliz Construction for initial two year terms with up to three one-year extension options for total contract amounts not to exceed $50,000,000. Approve the minutes for the October 1, 2026, Mobility Committee Meeting.
Identify items to be discussed at future meetings.
Discussion and possible action to set the Mobility Committee meeting dates for calendar year 2027.

Conduct a public hearing and consider an ordinance granting a site-specific amendment to City Code Chapter 25-8, Subchapter A, Article 13 (Save Our Springs Initiative), as minimally required to address development at the site located at 5811 Southwest Parkway located in the Barton Springs Zone. Funding: This item has no fiscal impact.

Conduct a public hearing to receive public comment on proposed amendments to City Code Chapter 25-2 (Zoning) that would allow up to three housing units, including tiny homes and recreational vehicles, on a single-family (SF) zoned property; revise regulations that apply to a property with two housing units; and remove restrictions on the number of unrelated adults living in a housing unit.

Approve an ordinance amending the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Austin Municipal Court Operating Budget Special Revenue Fund (Ordinance No. 20260812-007) to accept and appropriate $1,000,000 in grant funds from the U.S. Department of Justice Bureau of Justice Assistance FY25 Second Chance Act Pay for Success Initiative and authorize one full-time equivalent, grant-funded position for the Austin Community Court Rebuilding Families and Communities Initiative, a kinship-based reentry housing program. Funding: $1,000,000 is available from the U.S. Department of Justice Bureau of Justice Assistance through the FY25 Second Chance Act Pay for Success Initiative. A City funding match is not required.

Approve a resolution reappointing Tracy Thompson, Rajeev Thomas, Leslie Thorne, Greg Milligan, and Rustin Roussel to the Austin-Bergstrom Landhost Enterprises, Inc. Board of Directors, each for a term of six years beginning January 28, 2027.  Funding: This item has no fiscal impact.

Authorize negotiation and execution of an agreement with Digital Artist in an amount not to exceed $300,000 for the Northeast Service Center Suspended 3D Artwork for Art in Public Places Project. Funding: $300,000 is available in the Capital Budget of Austin Financial Services.
Approve the minutes of the Austin City Council regular meeting of November 5, 2026.

Approve proposed bylaws for the Austin Travis County Food Policy Board to increase county-appointed board member terms to four years.
Approve proposed bylaws for the Hispanic/Latino Quality of Life Resource Advisory Commission to add public safety to its purpose and duties.

Approve a resolution directing the City Manager to ensure social services contracts and grants are subject to the City’s standard procurement and grant policies, processes, and procedures, to update those policies, processes, and procedures as needed, to provide appropriate training, and to designate points of contact for social service vendors to navigate the contracting and grant processes.

Authorize negotiation and execution of an amendment to the agreement with Communities for Recovery to provide peer recovery counseling services for community intervention to prevent opioid overdoses by using evidence-based practices in opioid stewardship, opioid use disorder, and opioid harm reduction, to extend the agreement for a 12-month term through March 31, 2028, in an amount not to exceed $250,000, for a revised total agreement amount not to exceed $750,000. Funding: $250,000 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Opioid Settlement Fund Budget of Austin Public Health Department.

Authorize negotiation and execution of an amendment to an agreement with Central Texas Food Bank, Inc. for the College Food Access program, to provide services to college students in Austin/Travis County with limited access to food for a six-month term, through September 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $141,750, for a revised total agreement amount not to exceed $729,250. Funding: $141,750 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budget of Austin Public Health Department.

Authorize negotiation and execution of an amendment to an agreement with Austin Travis County Mental Health and Mental Retardation d/b/a Integral Care to provide substance misuse services to low-income individuals in Austin/Travis County for a 6-month term ending September 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $206,932, for a revised total agreement amount not to exceed $1,586,476. Funding of $206,932 is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budget of Austin Public Health Department.

Authorize approval of a resolution to appoint Shannon Jones as a voting member to fill a vacancy on the Austin/Travis County Public Health Commission Boards and Commission for a term to expire March 1, 2030, who will advise City Council on public health programs, projects and services within Austin and Travis County, and to waive the residency requirement in Section 2-1-21. Funding: This item has no fiscal impact.

Approve an ordinance amending the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Austin Public Health Operating Budget Special Revenue Fund (Ordinance No. 20260812-007) to accept and appropriate $300,000 in grant funds from St. David’s Foundation for the Citywide Supporting Perinatal Access, Care, and Equity collaborative. Funding: $300,000 is available from St. David’s Foundation. A City funding match is not required. A fiscal note is attached.

Funding: This amendment corrects an error in the adopted fee amount and has no fiscal impact on the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 budgeted revenue for Austin Planning, which was based on the correct fee amount.

Funding: This item is projected to result in an annual revenue of $100 in the Operating Budget of Austin Facilities Management.
